title: Sam Altman says OpenAI entering ‘new era of discovery’ with AI mathematics results
key_facts: OpenAI says an unreleased AI model solved 372 maths problems, published on GitHub.
Altman shared the blog post on X: 'We are entering a new era of discovery now'.
Results cover algebra, number theory, theoretical computer science, mathematical logic and topology.
Each result used on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute; the model was given roughly 4,000 problems.
Many proofs were checked with Lean; not all are peer reviewed.
OpenAI consults an advisory group on mathematics and AI at the Institute for Advanced Study.
OpenAI plans to fund workshops and conferences on understanding AI-produced results.
quote_evidence: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman shared the blog post on X.
Many of the proofs had been checked using Lean - a widely used proof-checking programme.
Though not all have been peer-reviewed yet.
why_it_matters_hint: A company claims AI is producing mathematical results at scale, still awaiting full outside review.
notes: CNBC TV18 page returned no text; read India Today (amp page) on the same story. India Today also says OpenAI solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Challenge last month and that a New York University professor said the company may have used his work; those are India Today's statements and are not repeated as fact. Other outlets give different counts (722); India Today's 372 is used.
